content:
vikram: heads up — p99 on host-side small-stream requests jumped ~30% after yesterday's kernel-packing change. saw it on canary and production sampling :eyes:
amy: link to the dashboard/screenshot?
vikram: https://dash.redwood/perf/1767 — look at grpc streaming bucket (50-200 token responses). p50 unchanged, p95 +10%, p99 +30%.
bench-bot: CI perf job 1767772468 finished. summary:
```
baseline: p99=124ms
new:      p99=162ms (+30%)
writev syscalls per request: baseline=6 -> new=24
cpu (host preparse): baseline=18% -> new=34%
```
chris: is this isolated to gRPC streaming? what about http chunked?
vikram: HTTP chunked shows some increase but much smaller. grpc streaming with many tiny frames is worst.
olivia: checked KV cache metrics — hit rates and eviction spikes are flat. not a kvcache regression. tokenization time per request up ~18% in profiler.
amy: any obvious hot functions?
vikram: profiler flame shows big delta in host ingress: `Ingress::assemble_frames` and `Tokenizer::normalize_utf8` spend more cycles. also more time in `writev_coalesce` path because small buffers pushed through. snippet:
```
# perf top-ish diff (hot stacks)
+  12.1%  libhostpreparse  Ingress::assemble_frames
+  9.8%   libtokenizer     Tokenizer::normalize_utf8
+  7.5%   libnet          writev (syscalls)
```
chris: suspicion: kernel-packing change altered memory layout so we lost some in-place parsing, causing extra copies. also might break MSG_MORE usage in the rust shim -> forces immediate syscalls.
vikram: agreed. I reproduced locally by toggling the kernel-affinity flag from the change: disabling it drops writev count back and reduces p99.
amy: small experiment ideas: try re-enabling in-place slice parsing, or restore previous buffer ownership semantics so tokenizer can operate without copying. also test coalescing at user-space: buffer writes with MSG_MORE (or `TcpStream::write_vectored` with `write()` hints) to reduce syscall rate.
olivia: +1 on user-space coalesce. we can add an adaptive micro-batcher that groups writes for up to 1ms or until buffer threshold. should save lots of syscalls for tiny responses.
chris: on the networking side we can try bumping TCP_NODELAY behavior? but that affects latency tail. better to coalesce on host.
bench-bot: triggered micro-batch canary job: `perf-canary/microcoalesce-176777` queued. will post numbers in ~20m.
vikram: plan:
- i will revert the kernel-packing tweak on a canary host and run the full workload.
- amy, can you run the micro-batcher patch on staging and bench-bot job?
- olivia, can you run a tokenizer micro-optim: avoid utf8 re-normalize when slice is already validated (cheap check)?
- chris, hold SRE alerting throttle for these hosts so we don't noise pager while we triage.
amy: running micro-batcher now, will update. :pray:
chris: i'll silence alerts for the canary pool. keep me posted if p99 starts going back up.
vikram: one more data point — tcpdump on the degraded canary shows many 40-80B frames per response. baseline had 1-2 frames. that's consistent with writev explosion.
olivia: if tokenizer change is non-invasive i can try a patch today. if it helps we should add a small unit test that ensures no extra copies in the hot path.
amy: thanks. if micro-batcher + tokenizer patch together get us within ~5% of baseline p99, we can re-enable kernel-packing behind a rollout flag and iterate.
vikram: cool. will post perf graphs and the revert diff once done.
bench-bot: canary job started: https://ci.redwood/jobs/perf-canary/microcoalesce-176777 (ETA 18m)
chris: acked. thanks team.
